text:
tara: Heads-up: raven-lite-int8 canary is producing duplicate funcall entries in the tool list for some prompts. Not parse-failures, but duplicate tool invocations (same name + args) which breaks idempotency for downstream handlers.

ben: That's bad for customers. How often and any obvious pattern?

tara: Around 1.2% on the e2e funcall set (~3k samples). FP16 baseline 0.05%. Duplicates appear mostly when responses are long and use kvcache prefix reuse. Example payload (trimmed):```{\"tools\": [{\"name\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":100}}, {\"name\":\"charge\",\"args\":{\"amount\":100}}]}``` Two identical entries back-to-back.

maria: Could be a streaming/chunk reassembly bug that replays the last tool when a KV cache prefix is appended. Have we seen this with other models?

sasha: We saw a similar duplicate emission class once when mirror+batch boundary caused replay of last token in a burst. Check whether duplicates correlate with CB boundaries or when mirror uses continuous KV reuse.

oliver: Also check the deterministic beam vs sampling config in the canary. High temperature + certain sampling picks can produce repeated tokens (e.g., verbatim repeats) but that usually shows as duplicate words, not structured tool arrays. This being exact-arg duplicates suggests a suffix re-emit.

tara: Repro command I used:```for i in $(seq 1 3000); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/invoke -d '{\"model\":\"raven-lite-int8\",\"prompt\":\"<billing-funcall-heavy>\",\"max_tokens\":400}' -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" | jq -r '.out' >> out.log; done; grep -c '\"charge\"' out.log; grep -E '\\{\"name\":\"charge\".*,\\{\"name\":\"charge\"' out.log | wc -l``` gave the delta counts above.

ben: Quick mitigation options: 1) de-duplicate tool entries in the proxy (soft fix), 2) reduce canary traffic and mirror to fp16, 3) disable CB on canary pool and replay, 4) enable an idempotency token field in tool args for canary routes so downstream can ignore repeats.

maria: For root cause, run a kvcache-boundary replay and enable low-level runtime trace around emission frames. Also compare streamed vs non-streamed outputs — streaming reassembly bug would show chunk-level dupes.

sasha: Also run a quant-bisect across recipes to see if a particular quant table introduces this: maybe a token merge changed such that bracket+comma sequences are tokenized differently and a re-emit bug gets triggered.

oliver: I'll take runtime traces and instrument emission frame numbers to see if the same frame ID is emitted twice. If it's a KV reuse bug, frame IDs will show identical origin.

tara: Deploy-bot: Canary raven-lite-int8 -> 30% at 3650000000, monitor: https://deploys.redwood/3650000000

deploy-bot: (auto) Canary alert threshold breached: duplicate-funcall-rate 0.9% at 3650000045

ben: Short-term: enable proxy dedupe + idempotency token for canary routes, scale down canary to 10%, keep fp16 mirror and replay logs attached to the incident. If proxy dedupe brings it under 0.2% we can keep investigating offline.

maria: Agreed. I'll run a replay with CB disabled and attach side-by-side diffs of emission frames and token ids. If no-CB drops duplicates significantly it's CB interaction.

oliver: Note — if we add proxy dedupe, be careful: some legitimate cases might intentionally call the same tool twice; dedupe should be per-consecutive-duplicate-within-window or based on an explicit idempotency key, not global.

tara: Update (20m): no-CB mirror dropped duplicates to 0.18% on 2k samples. Proxy dedupe reduced customer-facing duplicates to 0.03%. Looks like CB + kvcache replay is the main factor.

sasha: Great signal. Action items: 1) Keep proxy dedupe+idempotency for canary routes, 2) add kvcache-boundary and duplicate-emission checks to int8 onboard suite, 3) bisect quant recipes for tokenization changes, 4) schedule a runtime micropatch to guard against frame re-emit in CB path.

tara: Filing incident writeup and attaching traces + scripts. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
